content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate chips are small pieces of chocolate, usually shaped like tiny drops or discs. They are made from cocoa mass, sugar, milk (in the milk‑chocolate version), and sometimes added flavorings such as vanilla or salt. Chocolate chips are widely used in baking, desserts, and as a standalone snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chocolate chips were first introduced in the United States in the 1930s as a convenient way to add chocolate to cookies.
There are several types: dark, milk, white, and semi‑sweet.
Dark chocolate with a high cocoa content (70 % and above) is considered more beneficial because of its higher antioxidant levels.
Chips are often coated with a thin layer of sugar to prevent them from sticking together during storage.
In some countries chocolate chips are called “chocolate morsels” or “chocolate bits.”

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals and support heart health.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in chocolate supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron contributes to hemoglobin formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can improve mood.

items.title: Cognitive support
items.content: Flavonoids may help improve memory and concentration.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cocoa or other ingredients.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Milk and sweet varieties contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine and theobromine, which may affect sleep if consumed in excess.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Chocolate chips are high in saturated fats; people with elevated cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add chocolate chips to cookies, cupcakes, muffins, ice cream, yogurt, granola, and energy bars. They can be used as a topping for desserts or enjoyed in small portions as a sweet snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chocolate chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent melting and the formation of a white fat bloom.
